extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (petitioners/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for documenting prior-art/database searches on application file wrappers and for drafting/handling petitions to institute public use/on-sale proceedings under 37 CFR 1.292, including required content, timing, and examiner handling (prima facie determination, hearings, testimony schedule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record parent application refs with status
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the application number of a parent application that is still pending or abandoned, followed by “refs. checked” or “refs. ck’ed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If for any reason not all of the references have been checked because they are not available or clearly not relevant, such exceptions should be noted. Examples: 'S. N. 495,123 refs. checked'; 'S. N. 480,111 refs. checked except for Greek patent to Kam'; 'S. N.410,113 refs. not checked since the file was not available'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record patent number of related patented parent with refs status
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the patent number of a parent or related application that is now patented or of an original patent now being reissued with “refs. checked” or “refs. ck’ed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Pat. 3,900,000 refs. checked'; 'Pat. 3,911,111 refs. ck’ed'.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEARCH NOTES endorsement for computer/database searches
rubrics_metrics.description: In each action involving a search of a computer accessed text or chemical structure or sequence database, the examiner shall endorse, in the SEARCH NOTES box on the file wrapper flap, the name of the database service, the date when the search was made or was brought up to date and the examiner’s initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All entries shall be made in BLACK INK.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum documentation elements for computer database searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Computer database searches (text, chemical structure, or sequences) shall be documented in the SEARCH NOTES box on the file wrapper by providing the following minimum information: (1) The search logic or chemical structure or sequence used as a query; (2) The name of the file or files searched and the database service; (3) Date of the search; and (4) The examiner’s initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four elements are the minimum required information for documenting database searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable methods to provide required database-search documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Three ways in which the minimum documentation can be provided are: (1) supplying, and as necessary annotating, the computer search printout resulting from a computer assisted search; (2) recording the required information on the Search Request Form PTO-1590; or (3) recording the required information in the SEARCH NOTES box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For methods (1) and (2), the name of the database service and the expressions '(see form)' or '(see printout)' should be recorded in the SEARCH NOTES box as appropriate with the date and the examiner’s initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate or supplement printouts when history commands omit elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Most database services provide a command to display or print the search history which includes most, if not all, of the minimum required information. The missing elements may be documented by writing them on the printout of the search history or by supplying further portions of the search transcript which do include the missing elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some instances, depending on the database service, the log off command will supply the missing data element. A printout of the history command and log off response containing the required data elements is acceptable as full documentation of a search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate which search statements were reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are several search statements in the history, the statement or statements of which the results were reviewed should be indicated by circling them in BLACK INK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form or printout page(s) with the required data elements should be hole punched and placed in the application file on the right hand flap of the file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database-service-specific missing-element handling (Table 1 guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that individual database services differ in what the history command prints (search logic, date, file name, database service name). The missing elements identified for each service must be supplied by annotation, additional transcript, or log off output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: STN may not display the database service name with history and may require log off; WEST does not print the date of the search on some pages so date must be documented in writing. Consult Table 1 for per-service 'history command' and 'missing elements' behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printout handling and filing on file wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: Printouts (history command and relevant transcript portions) that contain required data elements should be hole punched and placed in the application file on the right-hand flap of the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If missing elements are supplied only by additional transcript pages, include those pages; circle reviewed search statements in BLACK INK; keep printouts with the file for later updating or review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search logic / structure / sequence documentation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Search Logic - generally a display of the search commands executed by the search software. For a structure or sequence search, this can be a printout of the structure or sequence used to query the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the search logic or the structure/sequence used as the query is recorded so searches can be repeated or updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name of file searched must be recorded (not just file number)
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of File Searched - the name of the collection of data accessed is required. The file number alone is not adequate documentation of a search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some services (e.g., Dialog) supply only a file number; in those cases, supply the file name in writing because the name of the file is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of search must be recorded
rubrics_metrics.description: Date of Search - the date the search was made must be recorded. Some services (WEST, Dialog, Orbit, Questel) do not display the date as part of the history command and it must be documented separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the history/printout lacks the date, write the date of the search on the printout or include transcript output that supplies the date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide and peptide sequence search documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide and peptide sequence searches will be fully documented by a printout of the search query sequence and the beginning of the search result file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each query sequence should be clearly related to the appropriate search result, if necessary, by appropriate annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for other public/locally accessed databases (CD-ROM etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: For other types of publicly accessible computer accessed databases (e.g., CD-ROM databases, specialized databases, etc.), record data as necessary to provide unique identification of material searched and sufficient information as to the search query or request so that the search can be updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record should also document the location of the database and its form (CD-ROM, etc.). Examples are provided for citing biotech and non-biotech CD-ROM databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information recorded on file wrapper vs. IDS notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain indications of consideration or nonconsideration of prior art citations submitted by applicant in Information Disclosure Statements are not recorded on the file wrapper; see MPEP § 609 for IDS handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not substitute SEARCH NOTES wrapper entries for IDS handling instructions; consult MPEP §609 for IDS-specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition entry formal requirements (37 CFR 1.292)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for institution of public use proceedings (37 CFR 1.292) and accompanying papers, or a notice that such a petition has been filed, shall be entered in the application file if: (1) The petition is accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(j); (2) The petition is served on the applicant in accordance with § 1.248, or filed with the Office in duplicate in the event service is not possible; and (3) The petition is submitted prior to the date the application was published or the mailing of a notice of allowance under § 1.311, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicate copies should be submitted only when, after diligent effort, it has not been possible for petitioner to serve a copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content and form of a public-use petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.292 must be submitted in writing, must specifically identify the application (application number or serial number and filing date), and should include a listing of all affidavits or declarations and exhibits relied on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must contain a sufficient description of the subject matter alleged to have been in 'public use' or 'on sale,' including any necessary photographs, drawings, diagrams, exhibits, or flowcharts to enable the examiner to compare the claimed subject matter to the alleged public-use/on-sale subject matter. The petition and accompanying papers must either (A) reflect service on applicant/attorney/agent, or (B) be filed in duplicate if service is not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended identifying information to include on petition
rubrics_metrics.description: When known, the following information should be placed on the petition: (A) Name of Applicant(s); (B) Application number; (C) Confirmation number; (D) Filing date of application; (E) Title of invention; (F) Technology Center art unit number; (G) Name of examiner to whom the application is assigned; (H) Current status and location of application; (I) The word 'ATTENTION:' followed by the area of the Office to which the petition is directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition, the petition itself should be clearly identified as 'PETITION UNDER 37 CFR 1.292.' If accompanied by exhibits/attachments, include identifying information on them to avoid separation or loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special marking and handling for 'REISSUE LITIGATION' petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a petition is directed to a reissue application for a patent which is involved in litigation, the outside envelope and the top right-hand portion of the petition should be marked with the words 'REISSUE LITIGATION' (preferably in a bright color).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given urgency, petitioners may hand-carry such petitions to ensure prompt receipt. In litigation-type cases, responses should be hand-carried to the appropriate area. A complete copy including all exhibits should be served on applicant/attorney/agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary handling by OPLA and timeliness considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition filed under 37 CFR 1.292 should be forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration (OPLA). OPLA staff will ascertain whether the formal requirements have been fulfilled, including whether the petition was filed prior to mailing of a notice of allowance under 37 CFR 1.311, whether the alleged use/sale occurred in this country more than 1 year before the effective filing date of the application, whether the petition contains affidavits/declarations/exhibits, whether papers have been filed in duplicate or served, and whether the required fee has been tendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit petitions as early as possible in the examination process so they receive maximum consideration. A petition cannot be considered after issuance as a patent or abandonment of the application; late petitions may be dismissed as untimely or moot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special timing rules for reissue-application petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition with regard to a reissue application should be filed within the 2-month period following announcement of the filing of the reissue application in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition cannot be filed within the 2-month period, a later-filed petition can be submitted but may not be entertained before examiner action. Requests for extension of the 2-month period must be filed as a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 and accompanied by the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(h), explaining the necessity. OPLA will critically review demonstrated need before granting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification search when petitioner cannot identify application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petitioner is unable to specifically identify the application but believes such an application to be pending, the petition should be directed to OPLA or 'Box DAC' with as much identifying data as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ex parte situations where a petitioner cannot identify the pending application by application number, the petition papers will be forwarded to the appropriate TC Director for an identification search. Once located, the application file should be forwarded to OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when service is not indicated or duplicate not filed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition does not indicate service on applicant and is not filed in duplicate, the Office will attempt to determine whether service has been made by contacting applicant or applicant’s attorney or agent. The Office may request petitioner to file a duplicate before referring to the examiner or may reproduce the petition in its sole discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition is not submitted prior to mailing of a notice of allowance it should not be entered in the application file; applicant should be notified that the petition is untimely and not entered. Specific handling: (A) If service of copy included, original petition should be discarded; (B) Where service not included, duplicate (if present) should be discarded and original sent to applicant along with notification of nonentry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's prima facie showing standard for public use petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A prima facie case is established by the petition if the examiner finds that the facts asserted in the affidavit(s) or declaration(s), as supported by the exhibits, if later proved true by testimony taken in the public use proceeding, would result in a statutory bar to the claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) alone or in combination with 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To make this determination the examiner must: identify exactly what was in public use or on sale; determine whether it was in use or on sale in this country more than 1 year before the effective filing date; and determine whether the pending claims 'read' on or are obvious over what has been shown to be in public use or on sale. Compare all pending claims with the matter alleged, not just claims identified by petitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions alleging obviousness must include prior art/explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: In situations where the petition alleges only that the claims are obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale, the petition should include prior art or other information on which it relies and explain how the prior art or other information in combination with the subject matter asserted renders the claims obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner is not expected to make a search in evaluating the petition. However, if the examiner is aware of prior art which, in his/her opinion, renders the claims obvious over the asserted subject matter, the examiner may determine that a prima facie case is established even if the petition alleged only anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner memorandum when prima facie determination made
rubrics_metrics.description: After making a determination, the examiner will forward a memorandum to the Patent Legal Administrator stating findings and decision as to whether a prima facie case has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings should include a summary of alleged facts, a comparison of at least one claim with the device alleged to be in public use or on sale, and any other pertinent facts to aid the Patent Legal Administrator. The report should be prepared in triplicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary hearing procedure and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner concludes that a prima facie case has been established, the Commissioner may hold a preliminary hearing. The parties will be notified of the time and date. No new evidence is to be introduced or discussed at this hearing; format is established by OPLA staff and Patent Legal Administrator presides; the examiner may attend only as an observer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ex parte cases, whether or not the examiner found a prima facie case, no copy of the examiner's memorandum will be forwarded to the petitioner. If the petition covers restrictable subject matter and petitioner is unaware of restriction, petitioner will be informed that the examiner’s conclusion is limited to elected subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use proceeding testimony rules and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: When public use proceedings are instituted, the examiner will set a schedule of times for testimony and for filing the record and briefs using specified intervals (e.g., petitioner testimony to close ~60 days; applicant objections ~20 days after; petitioner supplemental ~20 days after; applicant request for cross-exam ~20 days after; cross-examination ~30 days after; rebuttal testimony ~20 days after; record and exhibits due ~30 days after rebuttal; petitioner brief ~30 days after; applicant brief ~20 days after).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may agree on a different schedule provided the last brief is due no later than the specified date and a copy of the new schedule is filed. No extension of time will be permitted under 37 CFR 1.136(a); petitions to extend the last brief must be under 1.136(b). A certified transcript of a deposition must be filed in the PTO within one month after the date of deposition (37 CFR 1.678). All papers must be served per 37 CFR 1.248. Testimony is limited to issues of public use or on sale; no testimony will be received on whether the claimed subject matter would have been obvious over subject matter asserted to be in public use or on sale.
